en.title: The post office and parcels
en.summary: Sending letters and parcels, choosing a service and understanding delivery information.

paragraphs: The post office offers several services at different speeds and prices. This lesson helps you choose, describe a parcel and follow its progress.
A customer is sending a parcel from a post office in Glasgow to Spain.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: I would like to send this parcel to Spain.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Let me weigh it. It is two and a half kilos. What is inside?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Some books and a jumper. They are gifts.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Would you like first class or second class?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: The faster service takes three days, and the standard one takes about six. The faster service costs more.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: I will take the faster one. Can I track it online?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Yes, here is your tracking number. You will be able to see where the parcel is at any time.

paragraphs: **1. Send, weigh and track are the verbs of the post.** Learn their patterns: send something to someone. See Introduction to Grammar: Verbs and verb phrases.

blocks.html:
PatternExample
send + object + tosend a parcel to Spain
weighLet me weigh the parcel.
trackYou can track it online.
deliverIt will be delivered in three days.

paragraphs: **2. It takes with a length of time.** English uses It takes + time for the duration of a process, and it can take a question or a negative. See Introduction to Grammar: Present tense, being and having.

blocks.html:
FormExample
statementIt takes three days.
questionHow long does it take?
negativeIt doesn't take long.
comparisonThe faster service takes less time.

items: A stamp shows that postage has been paid.
Postcode is British and zip code is American.
Recorded delivery and registered post mean the parcel is signed for on arrival.
Customs may ask you to complete a form when sending abroad.

paragraphs: The Post Office in Britain also sells insurance, foreign currency and passport photographs. Many people now collect parcels from a locker or a neighbourhood shop instead of waiting at home.
